questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a country where English was the first language, and that the country was within Europe.

questions.answer: I did not need any assistance.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing was very close to campus, so it was easy to find.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was a part of the university so all students were students from the same university which made it easier to find friends as you could find people who were doing your course.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was very long, and the University were very slow with getting back to us with a confirmation of acceptance, modules etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You were able to contact the uni by email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3 out of 4 classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience. Make sure you do everything as soon as possible, because the sooner you complete the different steps the quicker you'll get through.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were for 3rd year students, but felt a bit complicated sometimes as an exchange student because of the language barrier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was very good and professors would be available if you needed help. The lectures were shorter (1 hour) compared to the lectures at UCPH, and they would have seminars/tutorials with up to 10 students, where the curriculum would be discussed. The classes were devided into "units", so after each unit there would be a tutorial/seminar which would sum up that unit and discuss everything. All classes during the unit would be lectures only, but where there was a chance to ask the professor questions too.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LW3591 Criminal Justice: Policing, Sentencing and Rehabilitation 2021-22 SEM1
LW3351 Criminology (Study Abroad) 2021-22 SEM1 
LW3271 Human Rights in the 21st century (Study Abroad) 2021-22 SEM1
LW3231 Employment Law (Study Abroad) 2021-22 SEM1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found Employment Law and Criminal Justice as the best courses. Employment law was so well structered, that the professors made sure you would be able to do the assessments without any struggle.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many options, compared to UCPH. There was a club available for every sport you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined non-academic activities based on my own personal preference and my beliefs so I can only recommend to join the activities which you're interested in as it will help expand your social circle.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The University offers a lot of activities during weekends and holidays, which you can join. If not, then going to other parts of the countries was how I spent most of my weekends and holidays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture in UK is very similar to the one in Denmark, but I got adjusted easily also because of the accommodation I stayed at, as the girls would tell me how they do certain things. For instance, in England they have eggs in their cupboard and not in the fridge.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My best advice will be to live somewhere with students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult that the busses were on the opposite side, as the driving in the UK is opposite to the driving direction in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very humble and helpful and they apologise way more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to socialise and give yourself time to do so
2. The University is very close to accommodation so I would recommend to stay at the uni accommodation.
3. It is a very multi cultural University so you'll meet a lot of people with different backgrounds

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is placed 20 minutes away from the main town.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a chance to be a part of physical teaching again and mostly the new friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To not get behind in studies. You get behind easily as they don't give work in the first two weeks, and then all of a sudden they load you with a lot of pages to read so it's difficult to make a routine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
